knowledge:
- key_parameters: formula=symbolic description of the null model to be fitted ;; pheno=data.frame containing the phenotype and covariates ;; grm_fn=GDS file name for the genetic relationship matrix ;; trait.type=type of the phenotype, e.g., "binary" ;; sample.col=column name for sample IDs in the phenotype data frame ;; mac=minimum minor allele count threshold for filtering variants ;; parallel=number of processes/threads for parallel computation ;; res.savefn=optional file path to save association results directly to a GDS file ;; use.gpu=logical, enables OpenCL-based GPU acceleration for GRM cross-product computation ;; geno.sparse=logical, defaults to TRUE for optimized CPU-only sparse genotype storage; set to FALSE for dense 2-bit packed genotypes to use GPU
- alternatives: SAIGE R package=SAIGEgds is 5 to 6 times faster in fitting null models and calculating p-values ;; SNPRelate=used for LD pruning (snpgdsLDpruning) before GRM construction ;; SeqArray=used for general GDS file manipulation (seqOpen, seqSetFilter, seqExport, seqClose, seqGetData)
- when_to_use: Use this package when performing large-scale genetic association studies (PheWAS/GWAS) with biobank-scale datasets (e.g., UK Biobank) to control for case-control imbalance and sample relatedness using mixed models, specifically when genotype data is in SeqArray GDS format.
- pitfalls: Building the null model with older versions of SAIGEgds (docs warn: "For more accurate model building, the null model should be built using SAIGEgds>=v1.9.1!") ;; GPU acceleration requires an OpenCL-compatible GPU and runtime, and only applies to dense genotypes (geno.sparse=FALSE). Sparse genotype storage (geno.sparse=TRUE, the default) uses an optimized CPU-only path ;; GPU memory allocation must not exceed 80% of device global memory, or it will fall back to CPU.

workflows.name: saige_association_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform single-variant association testing using generalized linear mixed models (GLMM) with SPA, including GRM preparation, null model fitting, and p-value calculation.
input: pheno (data.frame containing sample.id, phenotype, and covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Open GDS file and perform LD pruning using SNPRelate::snpgdsLDpruning ;; 2. Filter variants and export to a new GDS file for GRM using SeqArray::seqSetFilter and SeqArray::seqExport ;; 3. Fit the null GLMM model using SAIGEgds::seqFitNullGLMM_SPA ;; 4. Calculate association p-values using SAIGEgds::seqAssocGLMM_SPA ;; 5. Load and inspect results using SAIGEgds::seqSAIGE_LoadPval
workflows.code:
gds <- seqOpen(geno_fn)
snpset <- snpgdsLDpruning(gds)
snpset.id <- unlist(snpset, use.names=FALSE)
grm_fn <- "grm_geno.gds"
seqSetFilter(gds, variant.id=snpset.id)
seqExport(gds, grm_fn, info.var=character(), fmt.var=character(), samp.var=character())
seqClose(gds)
sampid <- seqGetData(grm_fn, "sample.id")
pheno <- data.frame(
    sample.id = sampid,
    y  = sample(c(0, 1), length(sampid), replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.95, 0.05)),
    x1 = rnorm(length(sampid)),
    x2 = rnorm(length(sampid)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
glmm <- seqFitNullGLMM_SPA(y ~ x1 + x2, pheno, grm_fn, trait.type="binary", sample.col="sample.id")
assoc <- seqAssocGLMM_SPA(geno_fn, glmm, mac=10, parallel=2)
seqAssocGLMM_SPA(geno_fn, glmm, mac=10, parallel=2, res.savefn="assoc.gds")
res <- seqSAIGE_LoadPval("assoc.gds")
